newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BKB sets up Zurich private banking office.
newsitem.headline: BKB sets up Zurich private banking office.

text.p: Basler Kantonalbank (BKB), one of Switzerland's 25 cantonal banks, is setting up a representative office in Zurich for private banking, bringing it into the region dominated by Zurich Kantonalbank (ZKB).
Werner Sigg, the bank's chief executive officer acknowledged to reporters that it was an unusual step, given that cantonal banks, with rare exceptions, stick to their home turf.
While some friction may be inevitable, he said it was necessary to be in Zurich to expand BKB's private banking.

"We naturally presented our plans to both the (cantonal banking) association, and the Zurich Kantonalbank. We didn't exactly get applause, but we were able to gain understanding for this step," Sigg said.
"Whoever wants to be grow in the area of private banking, must be present in Zurich," he added.
Zurich offers easier access to international clients, he said, noting the private banking sector would likely see fewer, but more efficient, competitors.
Sigg said that BKB, with a balance sheet total of roughly 11 billion Swiss francs, is ranked between sixth- and tenth-largest of the cantonal banks.

"We do not see ourselves as competition for the Zurich Kantonalbank," Sigg said. BKB's Zurich office, legally a division of the Basler parent, will serve only private clients. It has no plans to infringe on ZKB's retail banking business.
Zurich Kantonalbank is the largest of the cantonal banks, with 57.8 billion in assets.
Sigg said BKB would also be advertising the new private banking services, mainly outside of Zurich.
BKB has participation certificates listed on the Swiss exchange, but its main shareholder is the city-canton of Basle.
The move was also unusual in that the top staff at the new private banking division, including Hans Ringger, head of the Zurich operation, come from what was formerly Swiss Volksbank.
As part of a restructuring, Credit Suisse Group, formerly CS Holding, concentrated domestic operations in what was previously Volksbank in a new unit.
"In Switzerland, it is rather unusual for a whole team to change," Rinnger said. One attraction was BKB's efforts to build up its trading operations, he said.

BKB invested 20 million francs to build up its trading facilities in Basle and increased the number of staff in the area to 50 from 30. "This matches the needs of customers we wish to serve," he said.
